issue.title: Nothing installs ruff/mypy from uv.lock, so lint verdicts depend on install date: a lock-faithful venv reports F811/mypy findings CI does not
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-um.9.5.4 (note #10) during epic sase-um.9.5 ("Complete the
interrupted sase-um.9 release-gate landing"), routed to a task by sase-um.9.5.land on
2026-08-29.

`uv.lock` pins `ruff==0.15.4` and `mypy==1.19.1`, but nothing in the normal install path
installs from the lock. Both `just install` (Justfile:173,
`uv pip install --python ... --no-sources ... -e ".[dev]"`) and CI's setup resolve
`ruff` and `mypy` from `pyproject.toml`'s unconstrained `[dev]` entries
(pyproject.toml:62-63), so each install picks up whatever the index publishes that day.

The consequence is that lint verdicts depend on install date rather than on the tree.
An agent or contributor who builds a lock-faithful environment (`uv sync`, which is the
documented path in sibling repos and the path phase sase-um.9.5.5 used for bugyi-chops)
gets the older locked tools and sees F811 and mypy diagnostics that `just lint` and the
CI lint job do not report -- and the reverse is equally possible once the index moves
past whatever CI last resolved. Neither result is wrong; there is simply no single
declared answer to "which ruff and mypy define this repo's lint gate".

## Scope

Decide which source of truth wins and make the other agree, rather than patching one
symptom:

- If the lock is authoritative, install the dev toolchain from it (or pin ruff and mypy
  in `[dev]` to the locked versions) so a lock-faithful venv and CI run the same gate.
- If the floating index is authoritative, the lock's ruff/mypy entries should not be
  treated as reproducible and the discrepancy should be documented so nobody debugs a
  phantom lint failure again.

Either way the acceptance test is the same: create a fresh environment by the documented
path, run `just lint`, and get the same verdict CI gets on the same SHA.

task_type_fields.impact: Agents cannot trust a green local just lint to mean CI lint is green, or a red one to mean a real defect. Time is spent either fixing phantom findings or discovering real ones only after a CI round-trip.
task_type_fields.location: uv.lock (ruff 0.15.4 at line 1921, mypy 1.19.1 at line 1149) vs pyproject.toml:62-63 unconstrained [dev] entries and Justfile:173 uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
task_type_fields.repro: Observed while landing epic sase-um.9.5 on 2026-08-29: a lock-faithful local venv failed ruff F811 and mypy checks that the CI lint job passed on the same SHA. Confirm by creating one environment with uv sync (locked ruff 0.15.4 / mypy 1.19.1) and one with just install (index-resolved), then running just lint in each on the same commit.
